method: match the source window with every byte of an in-image dword marked as an operand, and rank candidates by their longest run of agreeing literals. The rule covers the operands that must move between two titles (call displacements into .text and absolute references into .data) while field offsets and immediates stay literal.
checks: the same-title round trip reports the source address as the single candidate, run = span
the oracle's memset fixture 0x46a720 matches th12 0x477420 with run = span and no other candidate in the image
0x456ad0 in th11 is a lone ret; the only run in th12 is the same lone ret at 0x4622e0

0x412e30 -> 0x004154d0 measured this round: prologue run 9 (ambiguous, two candidates) discriminated by the body window (run 21, unique) and by the frame size 0x310 vs 0x308; confirmed by the fixture suites calling it.

a code row must name an instruction boundary: 0x4569c0 -> 0x004621c0 re-measured with th-twin-fields.py (23/24 aligned, shape 1.000) after the +1 candidate target made the fixture's five-byte jump land inside the prologue and strand a pushed EBP on the stack

a row whose target is not the twin entrance is reported by tools/th-twin-rows.py; four rows (0x455a00 0x455df0 0x455bc0 0x456020 -> 0x0044bf6a) are withdrawn because th12 has no copy of them at all (the window that matched was a 129-fold shared logging prologue)

round 299 measured three of the 487 untranslated fixture literals and anchored them: 0x44b4b0 -> 0x00455630 (20/24 paired), 0x44fd10 -> 0x0045a3c0 (21/29), 0x452010 -> 0x0045cdf0 (41/42); 0x451ef0 was left out because its best candidate is the same target as 0x452010 at only 16/42, i.e. an alias, not a measurement

round 300 applied 81 batch rows under a strict rule (paired 1.000, >= 12 instructions, source not named by helpers.mjs) after a wider pass broke anm-load-all; 6 measurements were left in tools/tmp/twin-batch-300.json for individual verification

round 301 relaxed the wildcard scan (span 0x40, literal run 5) for the addresses round 300 could not resolve and applied 22 more rows under the same strict rule; 15 measurements were left aside for individual verification

round 302 added an entry-prefiltered fallback to the batch pass (a window match cannot reach a source whose literal run is short; every function entry is a candidate, prefilted on the first instruction bytes) and applied 11 rows (7 anchored, 4 measured); 4 measurements were left aside, including every aliased target whose two source windows differ

round 302 added --derive: an address inside an already-anchored function is the same-index instruction of its twin, verified on its own window; 6 rows were derived this way, resolving the first raw call of both laser suites
round 303 measured the ENCLOSING function entry of every unresolved mid-function address (8 entries); 6 were applied, and the addresses are then derived from them by instruction index

round 303 dropped 5 container rows that sat within 0x200 of an address helpers.mjs names: the exclusion is by region, because the enclosing entry of a harness address is a harness address eight bytes earlier
round 303 derived 2 queued mid-function addresses by instruction index from their enclosing entries and verified each on its own window

round 304 replaced the alignment-based entry index with a CALL-TARGET index (27554 real entries per image) for both the container pass and the fallback candidate list, and applied 4 enclosing entries; 0 measurements were left aside by the strict rule, the harness region or an alias
round 303 derived 3 queued mid-function addresses by instruction index from their enclosing entries and verified each on its own window
anchored: a run of 12 or more consecutive agreeing literal bytes is treated as anchored; rows below that are candidates for the port to confirm by running the oracle, since the engine functions with many absolute references have few adjacent literals
purpose: the oracle fixtures in tests/cpp name the addresses of the port's first title; these rows are the measured counterpart of each in th12

evidence: the fixture calls `replace(touch(0x4569c0), ...)`, which writes a five-byte jump over the mapped address; the address this row used to name, 0x004621c1, is one byte past the function's `push ebp`, so the guest executed that push and then the jump, leaving the pushed EBP on the stack - the stub's `ret` popped it and the guest ran into a zero-filled stack slot (measured: EBP == [esp] == 0x7effc48, bytes at EIP all zero)

re-measured with tools/th-twin-fields.py from both entries (span 0x60): 23 of 24 instructions aligned, 0.958 of the longer stream, 1.000 operand-shape agreement, 0 moved displacements, so th11 0x4569c0 and th12 0x4621c0 are the same function

the one-byte offset the earlier measurement took comes from a real title difference: th12 adds a `push esi` (0x4621c1 `56`) to th11's `push ebp; push edi`, which shifts every later address the window compares
